## Two Magnitude Estimates for the 1906 Earthquake

Two different approaches produced magnitude estimates of 7.7 and 7.9 for the 1906 earthquake. The estimates differ because they come from different ways of measuring earthquake size.

The seismic analysis suggested a magnitude of 7.7 and used recordings from 12 of the 96 observatories studied. A USGS re-evaluation of geodetic measurements estimated a magnitude of 7.9, based on changes in angles and distances between benchmarks.

The figures reflect distinct methods: one based on seismic recordings, the other on ground deformation measured geodetically.
